title: Trump: Agnes Bunn files a discrimination complaint against Fred Trump
description_short: Trump: Agnes Bunn files a discrimination complaint against Fred Trump
description_medium: Agnes Bunn filed a housing-discrimination complaint with New York City on February 9, 1970, naming landlord Fred Trump. The excerpt identifies apartments at 41-10 Bowne Street in Flushing, Queens, and says Bunn learned of them from a friend who lived there. The rest of her account and the city’s response are not included.
description_long: Agnes Bunn filed a formal complaint with New York City on February 9, 1970, alleging housing discrimination by Fred Trump. The excerpt identifies apartments at 41-10 Bowne Street in Flushing, Queens, and says a friend who lived at that address told her about them. The text ends before giving Bunn’s complete account of her housing inquiry or the conduct she alleged. The filing began an administrative complaint process; it is not itself a finding that discrimination occurred. The available details do not include the full complaint, the city’s response, or the outcome of any investigation or proceeding. Those records are needed to establish what Bunn alleged and how officials handled the case.

title: Trump: William Barr's father hires Jeffrey Epstein at Dalton School
description_short: Trump: William Barr's father hires Jeffrey Epstein at Dalton School
description_medium: Donald Barr, headmaster of New York’s Dalton School and father of William Barr, announced in February 1974 that he would leave at the end of the school year. The account says he later hired Jeffrey Epstein to teach mathematics and science that September. The hiring date, screening process, and school officials’ knowledge are not established.
description_long: Donald Barr, then headmaster of New York’s Dalton School, announced in February 1974 that he would leave his post at the end of the school year. The account says he later hired Jeffrey Epstein, who began teaching mathematics and science that September. William Barr was Donald Barr’s son, but that relationship alone does not establish his involvement in the hiring. The available summary does not give the date of the hiring decision, include employment records, or explain what school officials knew about Epstein at the time. The sequence is a departure announcement followed by Epstein’s appointment to a teaching job; claims about prior knowledge or wrongdoing require additional evidence.

title: Trump: Epstein's Early Empire: Maxwell, Mogilevich, Mossad, and the CIA
description_short: Trump: Epstein's Early Empire: Maxwell, Mogilevich, Mossad, and the CIA
description_medium: Jeffrey Epstein reportedly formed Intercontinental Assets Group Inc. on August 18, 1981, after leaving Bear Stearns. The account says he had been fired over unregistered investment sales and makes broader claims about the firm’s criminal and intelligence connections. Those claims are not substantiated by the company information provided.
description_long: The account dates Jeffrey Epstein’s formation of Intercontinental Assets Group Inc. to August 18, 1981, after his departure from Bear Stearns. It says he was fired for selling investments without registering the sales, then characterizes the new firm as specializing in transnational crime and government assets. The latter claims are not supported by corporate records or contemporaneous reporting in the material available here. No client, transaction, or government asset tied to the company is identified. The event can be described as the reported launch of a consulting firm, but the circumstances of Epstein’s departure, the company’s activity, and the asserted organized-crime or intelligence links remain unverified. Corporate registration, reporting about its clients, and evidence for those broader claims are needed to assess them.

title: Trump: Carl Icahn destroys industry giants, helps debilitate the Midwest
description_short: Trump: Carl Icahn destroys industry giants, helps debilitate the Midwest
description_medium: Carl Icahn acquired Trans World Airlines in 1985 after a contested takeover process. A Washington Post report that year covered TWA’s request for the U.S. government to block his hostile bid. The supplied account describes TWA as a major St. Louis employer but does not detail the takeover terms or its effects on workers and the regional economy.
description_long: Carl Icahn became the owner of Trans World Airlines in 1985 after a contested takeover. A Washington Post report published earlier that year was titled “TWA Asks U.S. to Block Icahn’s Hostile Takeover,” documenting the airline’s effort to obtain federal intervention. TWA was an important employer in St. Louis, but the available account does not describe the takeover terms or what happened to the company and its workers afterward. The headline characterizes Icahn’s business career as destroying industry and harming the Midwest; the materials here do not quantify job losses or regional economic effects. The takeover dispute and the broader claim about its consequences are distinct. Deal records and evidence about TWA’s later operations are needed to assess the claimed impact on employees and the city.

title: Donald Trump rapes his wife after scalp reduction surgery
description_short: Donald Trump rapes his wife after scalp reduction surgery
description_medium: Ivana Trump later described an alleged 1989 encounter with Donald Trump after his scalp-reduction surgery as “rape.” During their divorce proceedings, she gave an account later reported by journalist Harry Hurt III. Ivana clarified in 1993 that she had felt “violated” but did not mean rape literally or criminally; in 2015, she called the story without merit.
description_long: The account links an alleged 1989 encounter between Donald and Ivana Trump to his recovery from scalp-reduction surgery. During their divorce proceedings, Ivana described the encounter as “rape,” according to a later account by journalist Harry Hurt III. In a 1993 statement, she said she had felt “violated” but did not mean rape in a literal or criminal sense; in 2015, she said the story was without merit. These later clarifications are central to understanding the allegation. The account also discusses a Trump Organization lawyer’s 2015 claim that a spouse could not be raped; he later apologized, and the article notes that New York had criminalized marital rape before 1989. The allegation was not adjudicated as a finding of fact. The reports and statements document an allegation and subsequent clarifications, which should be considered together rather than treating the headline as a legal conclusion.

preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump rapes his wife after scalp reduction surgery

title: Trump: FBI reports on Semion Mogilevich's transnational organized crime operation
description_short: Trump: FBI reports on Semion Mogilevich's transnational organized crime operation
description_medium: An FBI report from August 1996 reportedly estimated that Semion Mogilevich’s transnational criminal organization had about 250 members, including associates in the United States, and noted links to people in the Russian government. The underlying report is not reproduced here, and no connection to Donald Trump is established.
description_long: An FBI report dated August 1996 reportedly described Semion Mogilevich and a transnational criminal organization with about 250 members, including associates in the United States. The account says the report also noted links to people in the Russian government. It does not reproduce the document or its qualifications, and a broader claim that organized crime controlled the Russian government is not established by the supplied synopsis. The record also does not connect the report or Mogilevich to Donald Trump or describe a business relationship between them. The report itself, its definitions and caveats, and corroborating material about the alleged government links are needed to assess the claims.
